memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'I will turn your cities into ruins and lay waste your sanctuaries, and I
will take no delight in the pleasing aroma of your offerings'"
- Lev 26:31 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is a striking and sobering thought. God says the day would come when
He would take no delight in their offerings. The people might still be
bringing sacrifices, still going through the religious motions — and God
would find no pleasure in them at all.

That should stop us. It is possible to keep up all the outward acts of
worship while God takes no delight in them. Religion can continue long
after the heart has left.

Dear reader, God has always cared about the heart behind the offering, not
just the offering itself. Through Isaiah He said, these people come near
to me with their mouth and honour me with their lips, but their hearts are
far from me (Isa 29:13). Through Amos He said, I hate, I despise your
religious festivals... away with the noise of your songs (Amos 5:21-23).

This is not because worship does not matter. It is because God will not be
fooled by worship that is only external. He looks past the sacrifice to
the heart offering it.

Jesus warned about honouring God with lips while the heart is distant
(Matt 15:8). The most sobering possibility in the Christian life is not
open rebellion but hollow religion — going through motions God no longer
delights in.

Ask yourself honestly today: is my worship coming from my heart, or only
from my habit? God does not want your performance. He wants you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is my worship coming from my heart or only from habit?
2. Have my outward acts of faith outlasted my inward love for God?
3. What would it look like to worship God with genuine heart again?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, forgive me for worship that is only external. I do not want to go
through motions You take no delight in. Draw my heart back, so my worship
is real. Amen.
